satellites.title: Sudden Realization in Ordinary Speech
satellites.evidence: The idiom 恍然大悟 names a sudden realization in ordinary language. It need not imply religious awakening or verified knowledge.

satellites.title: Sudden Awakening, Sudden Practice
satellites.evidence: The Platform Sutra makes 頓悟 its watchword: 自性自悟，頓悟頓修，亦無漸次 — “one’s own nature awakens itself; awakening is sudden, practice is sudden, and there are no gradual stages.”
satellites.caveat: This is the Yuan edition in the Taishō; the Dunhuang manuscript is shorter. The sudden–gradual opposition is partly the polemic of the later Southern school.
